positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
In preparation for an upcoming user study, I conducted developmental work on  IAGO (Interactive Arbitration Guide Online), a platform for designing AI agents that can negotiate with humans. The purpose of the study is to test the effect of two factors on people’s decisions in a negotiation: modality and framing.

Throughout the course of this project, I utilized java to improve the agent v.s. agent interaction, refactor the foundational code, construct a system where humans are able to design their own negotiating agents, and redesign the user experience of the platform for the participants.

positions.title: Mobile Application Developer
positions.description:
Inspired by the computer game I helped create in January 2020, two other students and I have developed an IOS mobile app called Vroomba Wars. Now available on the app store! 

Vroomba Wars:
Why clean your room in real life when you can have a virtual "Vroomba" clean your virtual room? Race against time as you clear each room while avoiding pesky obstacles. Buy yourself more time by charging your battery in between tasks. You’ll find that it is harder than it looks!

As the lead programmer and lead visual artist, I became well versed in Swift and Spritekit, designed the user experience and interface of the app with Figma, created all the pixel art displayed with Photoshop, gained experience in the process of user testing and uploading the app to the Apple AppStore. By solving challenges such as collisions handling, random spawning, keeping track of high scores, and more with Swift, I have been able to grow more experienced as a coder and game developer.

Currently, we are working to expand the game by adding a multiplayer option to our game. In the multiplayer version, players will have a balloon attached to their Vroomba and will need to collide with each other to pop the balloon. Players will be able to play on their own devices, battling each other in real-time while being connected to the same WiFi network.

positions.title: Summer Research Intern
positions.description: The Interaction Lab focuses on developing computational principles and techniques to enable socially assistive human-robot interaction. The goal of Socially Assistive Robotics (SAR) is to improve user health and wellness, communication, learning, and autonomy. The project I’ve been working on in the lab is NRI Kids: “Socially Aware, expressive, and personalized mobile remote presence: co-robots as gateways to access to K-12 in-school education”,  which explores the educational experience, social dynamics, and design features of telepresence robots for homebound students. Throughout the project, I have visualized survey data collected from the participating students, teachers, and classmates in order to identify unique trends or findings from the experiment.

Academic Profile:

Demographics:

honors.title: Bunche Scholar
honors.description: The Ralph J. Bunche Scholars Program, named in honor of Nobel Prize-winning diplomat and civil rights activist Ralph J. Bunche, offers a select group of students of color exclusive access to leadership development opportunities and grants for independent scholarship, internships, or humanitarian projects. Bunche Scholars are recognized for their demonstrated academic achievement and community involvement. They are leaders in their communities and often exhibit a deep commitment to social justice and civic engagement.
